reasons: Deviation is correctly identified: Article III vests all right, title and interest in the Licensed Technology and its IP in Licensor, the broad 'Derivative Work' definition (1.3) sweeps in additions/enhancements, and Article VII(b) contemplates Licensee paying for customization (including a unique client front end) with no ownership or assignment to Licensee and no reservation of Licensee data rights — squarely short of the IP rule's preferred position.

Redline is directionally correct and minimal: it leaves Licensor's ownership of its pre-existing Platform/Licensed Technology intact and adds a 'Notwithstanding the foregoing' carve-out that (i) reserves Licensee ownership of its trading, order, client and account data, (ii) assigns paid-for customization deliverables to Licensee with a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence back of embedded Licensor IP, and (iii) disclaims joint ownership — covering all three limbs of the redline guidance.
No assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Licensor remains, so the walk-away trigger is cleared; deterministic checks confirm the operation applies cleanly.

Comment is accurate to the cited text (Article III, 1.3, Article VII(b)), uses the required prefix and first-person-plural professional tone, explains the change and cites the playbook position, and offers the fallback (Licensor ownership plus perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense).
Ancillary addition that Licensor may use Licensee Data only to perform its obligations is a proportionate corollary of the data-ownership reservation and does not constitute material scope creep.
